clue.text: Pound fare for travellers here

definitions.meaning: to pound is to batter or strike repeatedly
the refreshment car on a train or a station counter where passengers get food

explanation.definitionFit: Batter and strike are synonyms of pound; the other sense is a railway refreshment counter serving food to passengers.

clue.text: Take no action when model gets drunk

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone advises doing nothing while the fashion model gets inebriated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay put and wait rather than act or move.

clue.text: Care for retired old lady holding on to cleaner successfully

parts.note: to care for something is to like it

indicators.note: holding on to means the turned-round word grips the cleaner inside it
retired means drawn back, so the word for old lady is read backwards

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, MA
a char is a British cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A retired old woman clings to her housekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the old lady round, and 'holding on to' wraps her around the cleaner. A char (charwoman) is an old British term for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly, with complete success, as if by magic.

clue.text: What Indian may observe backed up by German agreement

indicators.note: backed means set going backwards, so the word up is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: An Indian custom is supported by a German saying yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns UP into PU. Puja is a Hindu act of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A puja is a Hindu ritual of worship, something a devout Indian observes.

clue.text: Unfamiliar shop husband's discovered in city

parts.note: unfamiliar means new

indicators.note: discovered in means the husband is found inside the shop word

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen shop
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband is found in a strange shop somewhere in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Survivor left behind on island extremely confident

indicators.note: behind means the left letter follows the word for on

parts.note: re means on, about or concerning

indicators.note: extremely points to the two extreme letters of confident

explanation.surface: Someone left stranded on an island stays thoroughly self-assured.
explanation.definitionFit: A relict is a surviving remnant, such as a species left over from an earlier age, or a widow.

clue.text: Huge change in game of two halves

indicators.note: change in tells us the word game is altered
of two halves says the change is swapping the word's two halves round

explanation.surface: A big shift in a football match that famously has two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: GAME split as GA and ME, the halves swapped. 'A game of two halves' is a football cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal for enormous or very great.

clue.text: Dodgy lawyer losing head — one with a fit of madness

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the lawyer word drops off

parts.note: a shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer loses his mind and has a mad fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the S off SHYSTER, leaving HYSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is an uncontrolled outburst of emotion, a wild frenzy.

clue.text: Message sent by European member cutting one form of public transport

indicators.note: cutting means the European member splits the transport word open

parts.note: a tram runs on rails in city streets
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A message is delivered by a European MEP who interrupts the tram service.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph and delivered on paper.

clue.text: Egg on endlessly served fast food item

indicators.note: endlessly means both end letters of the fast food word are removed

parts.note: a burger is a staple of fast food

explanation.surface: Someone is goaded into eating a burger served without end.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to encourage or spur them, which is to press or impel them.

clue.text: Old relation's memory described by doctors

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, a link; old relation is grandfather

indicators.note: described by means the doctors draw a line round the memory word

parts.note: GPs are general practitioners, family doctors
RAM is computer memory

explanation.surface: An elderly relative's recollections are written up by his physicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Gramps is a familiar name for a grandfather, an old relation.

clue.text: Officer about to pass out notes we hear on Armistice Day

definitions.text: notes we hear on Armistice Day

indicators.note: about means the officer letters go around the rest

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

indicators.note: out means the words to pass are put out of order

explanation.surface: An officer is close to fainting while a bugle call sounds at the remembrance service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TO PASS, and 'about' wraps the officer round it. Armistice Day (11 November) commemorates the war dead, and the bugle call closes the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call played at remembrance ceremonies to honour the fallen.

clue.text: Touch instrument the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the instrument is written backwards

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: Someone handles a musical instrument incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut adjoin, touching at a common border.

clue.text: Blend of tea with name review spelt wrongly

indicators.note: spelt wrongly means these letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A tea blend's name is misspelt in a critic's review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelt wrongly' rearranges TEA, N and REVIEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To interweave is to weave together, a synonym of blend or intermingle.

clue.text: Lines about a single Italian

indicators.note: about means the lines word goes around the single word

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry
a single means one

explanation.surface: Poetic lines are written concerning one unmarried Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese was a Renaissance painter from Verona in Italy.

clue.text: Loving having money in case of trouble

indicators.note: in case of means the money sits inside the trouble word as a case

parts.note: to dog is to trouble or plague
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Fond people keep money aside in case something goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means showing excessive fondness, an adoring kind of loving.

clue.text: Bring together a French couple (not married)

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: not tells us the married letter is left out of the couple word

parts.note: an item is a romantic couple

explanation.surface: A French couple who never wed are united.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes M from ITEM, leaving ITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join or combine, bringing parts together.

clue.text: Range needed by decidedly English singer

parts.note: a field is a range or scope
far means decidedly, as in far better

explanation.surface: An expanse is required by a very English vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush, and birds are songsters in crosswords.

clue.text: Deal with animals that have turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the animal words read bottom to top

parts.note: an elk is an animal
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Someone must handle creatures that have appeared unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ELK and CAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to deal with it or confront it.

clue.text: Succeeded — cooked the top Milanese dish

indicators.note: cooked means the words that follow are reworked into new order

explanation.surface: Success: the best Milan chef prepared a fine dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges THE TOP MILANESE; 'Milanese dish' misleads, as the dish is from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish omelette is a potato and egg dish, the tortilla.

clue.text: Tree Commission met around St David's Day

indicators.note: around means the commission word goes round the date

parts.note: a task is a commission or assignment
St David's Day, patron saint of Wales, falls on 1 March, MAR I

explanation.surface: A committee assembled about a Welsh saint's festival.
explanation.walkthrough: St David's Day is 1 March, written MAR I. 'met' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a shrub or small tree of salty coastal soils.

clue.text: This writer's three-quarter length coat is at bottom of drive

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, so this writer's is I'm

indicators.note: three-quarter length means the coat word keeps three of its four letters

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's coat

explanation.surface: The setter's short coat sits at the end of a driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarter length' drops the last letter of PELT. In a down clue the coat is 'at bottom'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to push or urge forward, to propel or drive.

clue.text: Seizure and unlawful access impressing one judge

indicators.note: impressing means the computer word presses the one and judge into itself

parts.note: hacking is unlawful access to computers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A theft and computer break-in so impress a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Hijacking is the seizure of a vehicle or aircraft by force.

clue.text: Appalling times during era celeb recollected

indicators.note: during means the multiplication sign sits within the rearranged letters
recollected means the words era celeb are gathered up again in new order

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A dreadful period in which a celebrity recalls past times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' rearranges ERA CELEB into EECRABLE; 'during' puts X after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means extremely bad, abominable or appalling.

clue.text: 4 fellows following say, funnily, in film

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 4 down, here meaning gear or kit

indicators.note: in means the say-funnily word and the fellows go inside the film

parts.note: ET is a Spielberg film

indicators.note: following means the fellows come after the witty word

parts.note: to quip is to say something wittily
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Four men come along after making a joke in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is gear, the kit used for an activity like fishing.

clue.text: Abandoned pier isn't in perfect condition

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A derelict jetty is not in good repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine means unspoilt, as fresh as new.

clue.text: When scandal upset girl abroad

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the scandal word is read backwards

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

explanation.surface: A foreign girl when a scandal disturbed her.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a Scandinavian girl's name, so a girl from abroad.

clue.text: Bread made in Aussie flat shortly after rising

indicators.note: after means the Aussie word follows the trimmed flat word
shortly means cut short, so the flat word loses its last letter

parts.note: matt means flat, not glossy

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the Aussie word reads upwards

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia

explanation.surface: Bread baked in an Australian apartment shortly after getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts MATT to MAT, and 'rising' turns OZ into ZO.
explanation.definitionFit: Matzo is unleavened bread eaten at Passover.

clue.text: Cardinal virtues finally believe it or not

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of virtues

parts.note: even expresses surprise, as in he even paid

explanation.surface: Believe it or not, the virtues finally become cardinal ones.
explanation.walkthrough: There are seven cardinal virtues, which leads the eye to 'virtues' as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal number is a counting number such as this one.
